meaning: to lessen in intensity or degree
mnemonic: "A Bait" -> "A bait to lessen the fish's struggle": when you use a bait, it often calms the fish, causing it to abate its struggle against being caught.
hinglish: "A Bait" -> "Ek bait se machhli ka struggle kam hota hai": jab aap machhli ko bait dete hain, toh uska struggle abate hota hai.

meaning: deviating from the norm or what is expected
mnemonic: "A Bearant" -> "A Bear Ant": imagine a bear wearing an ant costume, which is an aberrant sight in the animal kingdom. His actions were so bizarre that they were considered aberrant by all the other animals.
hinglish: "A Bearant" -> "A Bear Ant": ek bhaloo jo ek chiti ka costume pehne hue hai, yeh ek vichlit (aberrant) drishya hai jo sabko hairaan kar deta hai.

meaning: to assist or encourage someone to do something wrong or illegal
mnemonic: "A Bet" -> "A Bet on Wrongdoing": if you place a bet on someone to succeed in their wrongdoing, you are abetting them in their actions.
hinglish: "A Bet" -> "A Bet Lagana": agar aap kisi ko galat kaam karne me madad karte hain, to aap unhe abet kar rahe hain.

meaning: a state of temporary inactivity or suspension
mnemonic: A + 'Bay' + 'Once': when a boat is in a bay, it might stay there for a while, in abeyance, until the waves calm down and it can set sail again.
hinglish: A + 'Bay' + 'Once': jab ek nauka ek khadi mein ruk jati hai, woh kuch samay ke liye abeyance mein hoti hai jab tak lehar thik nahi hoti.

meaning: to regard with disgust and hatred
mnemonic: Abhor -> A + Bore: when something is so boring, you abhor it because it makes you feel disgusted.
hinglish: A + Bore: jab koi cheez itni bore ho jati hai ki aap usse ghusna karte hain, tab aap usse abhor karte hain.

meaning: to accept or act in accordance with something
mnemonic: "A" + "Bide" (to stay): if you agree to abide by the rules, you are staying true to them and following them.
hinglish: "A" + "Bide": agar aap niyam ka palan karte hain, toh aap un par baithe rehkar unka palan kar rahe hain.

meaning: extremely bad, unpleasant, and degrading
mnemonic: Ab +ject: when you are abject, it's as if you were 'ab' (away) + 'ject' (thrown), meaning you're thrown away into a miserable state.
hinglish: Ab + ject: jab aap ab ject hain, aap itne bechari hote hain ki jaise aapko 'ab' (door) + 'ject' (fek diya) kiya gaya ho, matlab aapki halat bekar hai.

meaning: to renounce or reject a belief or claim formally
mnemonic: Ab + Jure (juror): when a juror abjures their duty, they formally reject their role in the case, thus abjuring the responsibility.
hinglish: Ab + Joor: jab koi insaan ab joor (chhod) deta hai apne vishwas ko, toh wo usse tyag raha hai.

meaning: to exist in great numbers or quantities
mnemonic: A + Bound: animals 'abound' in nature, running freely without bounds in the wild.
hinglish: A + Bound: junglon mein jaanwar 'abound' karte hain, bina kisi bandhan ke khule mein daudte hain.

meaning: having a rough surface that can wear away or irritate
mnemonic: "Abrasive" -> "A Brash Wave": like a wave crashing harshly onto a shore, an abrasive texture can cause irritation or damage.
hinglish: "Aabra" + "Sive": jab kuch cheezein khurduri hoti hain, wo humein tang karti hain, jaise ek abrasive surface.

meaning: in line with or alongside, especially in relation to others
mnemonic: A + Breast: when people are side by side, they can be said to be 'a breast' apart, always keeping abreast of one another.
hinglish: A + Breast: jab do log ek sath chal rahe hote hain, tab unhein 'a breast' kehna sahi hota hai, kyunki ve hamesha ek dusre ke saath hote hain.

meaning: to repeal or do away with a law or agreement
mnemonic: Abrogate -> 'Ab' (away) + 'rogate' (from 'rogare', to ask): to abrogate is to take away the request or law, effectively ending its existence.
hinglish: Ab + Rogate: jab sarkar kisi kanoon ko radd karti hai, toh wo ab rogate karti hai, yaani uss kanoon ko khatam karti hai.

meaning: to leave secretly and hide, especially to avoid legal prosecution
mnemonic: Abscond -> 'Abs' (muscle group) + 'Con' (to con someone): when you con someone, you might abscond from the scene to avoid getting caught.
hinglish: Abs + Con: jab aap kisi ko con karte hain, toh aap gaye hote hain bina kisi ko bataye, yaani aap abscond karte hain.

meaning: to refrain from doing something
mnemonic: "Abs" + "Tame": if you want to have abs, you need to tame your cravings and abstain from junk food.
hinglish: "Ab" + "Stain": agar aapko achhe results chahiye, toh aapko unhealthy khanon se stain nahi karna chahiye, yani abstain karna hoga.

meaning: relating to ideas and concepts rather than physical objects; not concrete
mnemonic: Abstract -> 'A' + 'Bstract' (like 'abstract ideas'): when discussing ideas that aren't grounded in reality, you're dealing with the abstract.
hinglish: A + Bstract (जैसे 'अव्यवहारिक विचार'): jab aap kisi aise idea ki baat karte hain jo haqeeqat se juda hota hai, tab aap 'abstract' ki baat kar rahe hain.

meaning: difficult to understand; obscure
mnemonic: "Abstruse" -> "Abstract Use": when concepts are too abstract and complex, they can become abstruse and hard to grasp.
hinglish: "Abstruse" -> "A Bhoot Roose": jab koi bhoot itna ghoor se aaye ki samajh nahi aaye, toh woh abstruse hai.

meaning: to make something more noticeable or prominent
mnemonic: "Accent" + "uate": when you accent something, you make it more noticeable; similarly, to accentuate means to highlight or emphasize.
hinglish: "Accent" + "uate": jab aap kisi cheez ko accent karte hain, to aap use zyada noticeable bana dete hain; is tarah accentuate ka matlab hai highlight ya emphasize karna.

meaning: capable of being reached or entered
mnemonic: "Access" + "Able": If something is accessible, you are able to access it freely, just like walking into an open door.
hinglish: "Access" + "Able": Agar koi cheez accessible hai, toh aap us tak aasanai se pohonch sakte hain, jaise khuli darwaze se andar jana.

meaning: enthusiastic approval or praise
mnemonic: "A Clam" -> "A Claim": if you hear a clam making a claim, it’s probably something great, leading to acclaim. The author received acclaim for her work, much like a clam claiming the best shell.
hinglish: "A Clam" -> "A Claim": agar a clam koi claim kare, toh wo zaroor koi badi baat hogi, jisse acclaim milega. Us lekhika ko uski kitab ke liye acclaim mila.

meaning: a state of agreement or harmony
mnemonic: A + Cord: an agreement acts like a cord that ties together different ideas or parties in accord.
hinglish: A + Cord: ek samjhauta jaise ek cord hota hai jo alag alag ideas ya parties ko ek saath bandhta hai.

meaning: a person who assists a leader in a religious service or other activity
mnemonic: "Acolyte" -> "A Call Light": when you hear the 'call' for help, you might see an acolyte rushing to assist in the service.
hinglish: "A Call Light" -> "A Call for Light": jab kisi ko roshni ki zarurat hoti hai, to acolyte uss roshni ko lekar aata hai, jaise ki ek pooja mein.

meaning: to agree or express agreement silently or without protest
mnemonic: "A Quiet Yes" -> "Acquiesce": when you quietly agree to something without protest, you acquiesce.
hinglish: "A Quiet Yes" -> "Acquiesce": jab aap chup chaap kisi baat par sahmat hote hain, to aap acquiesce karte hain.

meaning: having a strong desire to acquire more wealth or possessions
mnemonic: "A + Quisitive": when you're 'a' person who is curious ('quisitive') about acquiring, you become acquisitive, always wanting more.
hinglish: "A + Kvisitive": jab aap 'a' insaan hain jo cheezein kharidne ke liye 'kvisitive' hain, toh aap 'acquisitive' hain, hamesha zyada chahte hain.

meaning: angry and bitter in speech or tone
mnemonic: "Acre" + "moan" (sound like 'moan' when bitter): when the discussion turns acrimonious, people often just moan about each other's harsh words.
hinglish: "Acre" + "moan": jab discussion itna acrimonious ho jata hai, log bas ek doosre ki kadi baatein sun kar moan karte hain.

meaning: the ability to make good judgments and quick decisions, typically in a particular domain
mnemonic: "Acu" (sharp) + "Men": sharp-minded men have great acumen in making decisions, especially in business.
hinglish: "Acu" (teekha) + "Men": teekhe mardon ki business acumen unhe jaldi sahi faisle karne me madad karti hai.

meaning: for a specific purpose or situation; not planned in advance
mnemonic: Ad + Hoc (this): when you need something 'ad hoc', you create it 'on the spot' for a specific purpose.
hinglish: Ad + Hoc (yahan): jab aapko kisi khaas kaam ke liye 'ad hoc' kuch banana ho, toh aap use bina kisi planning ke turant bana lete hain.

meaning: highly skilled or proficient
mnemonic: Adept -> A Deft Expert: she is adept at playing the violin, showcasing her deft skills.
hinglish: Adept -> A Deft Expert: woh ek adept musician hai jo bina kisi mushkil ke bahut saare instruments bajati hai.

meaning: to stick to something or remain attached
mnemonic: Adhere -> Add here: when you add glue here, things tend to adhere to each other, sticking together.
hinglish: Add + Here: jab aap cheezon ko yahaan chipkane ke liye paste karte hain, woh adhere kar jaate hain.

meaning: to scold or reprimand someone firmly
mnemonic: "Ad" + "Monish" (to warn): when you admonish someone, you are giving them a firm warning to correct their behavior.
hinglish: "Ad" + "Manish" (to warn): jab aap Manish ko admonish karte hain, toh aap usse uski galtiyon ke liye sakht warning dete hain.

meaning: clever or skillful in using the hands or mind
mnemonic: A + Droid: imagine a robot (droid) that is skillfully assembling gadgets with precision; that's what being adroit means.
hinglish: A + Droit: socho ek aadmi (droit) jo apne haath se chaturai se kaam kar raha hai; usse hum adroit kehte hain.

meaning: to make something poorer in quality by adding another substance
mnemonic: Adulterate: 'Add' + 'Alter': when you add something inferior to a product, you alter its purity, thus adulterating it.
hinglish: Add + Alter: jab aap kisi cheez mein kuch kharab cheez milate hain, toh aap uski asliat ko alter karte hain, yani adulterate.

meaning: having a negative or harmful effect
mnemonic: Adverse -> 'Adverse' (Against): when conditions are adverse, they work against your plans, like bad weather ruining a picnic.
hinglish: Adverse -> 'Adverse' (Against): jab mausam adverse ho, tab wo aapke plans ke against hota hai, picnic ke beech mein barish aane ki tarah.

meaning: to publicly support or recommend
mnemonic: Advocate -> Add + Vote: when you add your voice to a cause, you advocate for it.
hinglish: Add + Vote: jab aap kisi cause ko support karte hain, tab aap uski advocate karte hain.

meaning: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty
mnemonic: Aesthetics -> Aesthetic + 'Thetic' (related to): The aesthetic appeal of her painting was highly praised for its beauty.
hinglish: Aesthetic + 'Sthit' (situation): Uski painting ka aesthetic sthit hamesha sabko pasand aata hai.

meaning: a superficial or affected manner; a behavior intended to impress others
mnemonic: Affect + Action: her exaggerated affectation was just an action to seem more sophisticated than she really was.
hinglish: Affect + Action: uski affectation sirf ek action thi, jisse woh apne aap ko sophisticated dikhana chahti thi.

meaning: a natural liking or attraction to someone or something
mnemonic: A + Finity (infinite connection): they felt an affinity, as if their bond was infinite and unbreakable.
hinglish: A + Finity: unki dosti mein ek aisa khichav tha jaise woh ek dusre ke liye infinite hai.

meaning: having a great deal of money; wealthy
mnemonic: "Aflu" -> "A Few Lucrative": if you have a few lucrative investments, you become affluent and wealthy.
hinglish: "Aflu" + "A Few Lucrative": agar aapke paas kuch lucrative business hain, toh aap affluent ban jaate hain.

meaning: an action or remark that causes outrage or offense
mnemonic: "A Front" -> "A Front Row Seat": sitting in the front row allows you to see everything, but if someone throws a rude comment your way, it feels like an affront to your personal space.
hinglish: "A Front" -> "A Friend": agar aapke dost aapke samne koi beizzati karte hain, toh wo aapko ek 'affront' mehsoos karata hai.

meaning: to increase in power, status, or wealth
mnemonic: "A Grand Eyes" -> "A Grand Prize": when someone tries to aggrandize themselves, they want to make themselves look grand and deserving of a prize, often by exaggerating their achievements.
hinglish: "A Grand" + "Eyes": jab koi vyakti khud ko aggrandize karta hai, wo chahta hai ki log uski taraf badi aankhein kholein, jaise ki wo bahut khaas hai.

meaning: filled with shock or horror
mnemonic: "Aghast" -> "A Ghost": seeing a ghost is so shocking that it leaves you aghast in horror.
hinglish: "Aghast" -> "A Ghost": ek bhoot dekhkar sab log itne aghast hote hain ki unhe samajh nahi aata kya karein.

meaning: to stir up or disturb emotionally or physically
mnemonic: "Agitate" -> "A Gita" (a religious text): If you read the Gita and don't find peace, it may agitate your thoughts instead.
hinglish: "A Gita" (एक गीता): Agar aap ek Gita padhen aur shanti na mile, to yeh aapke vicharon ko agitate kar sakta hai.

meaning: cheerful readiness or willingness to do something
mnemonic: A + LACK + CRITIC: if you lack a critic, you tackle tasks with alacrity, showing your eagerness to succeed.
hinglish: A + LACK + CRITIC: agar tumhare paas koi critic nahi hai, toh tum kaam me alacrity se lagte ho, apni ichha dikhate ho.

meaning: to cause someone to feel isolated or estranged
mnemonic: "Alien" + "Late": if you feel like an alien, you might be late to understanding social cues, which can alienate you from others.
hinglish: "Alien" + "Late": agar aap alien ki tarah mehsoos karte hain, toh samajh nahi paane se aap late ho jaate hain, jo aapko dusron se alag kar sakta hai.

meaning: including everything or everyone; comprehensive
mnemonic: All + Encompass: when you encompass everything, you are all-encompassing; like a blanket that covers every part of a bed.
hinglish: All + Khaas: jab aap sab kuch include karte hain, tab aap all-encompassing hote hain; jaise ek blanket jo bed ke har hisse ko dhak leti hai.

meaning: symbolic; representing ideas or qualities through metaphorical figures or events
mnemonic: "All" (each) + "Egory" (category): in an allegorical story, every character or event belongs to a category that symbolizes deeper meanings.
hinglish: "Sab" (all) + "Rang" (color): ek allegorical kahani mein har rang ek vishesh bhavna ya soch ko darshata hai.

meaning: to make something less severe or intense
mnemonic: "A levitate" -> "A Lift to Create a Date": When you alleviate someone's pain, it's like lifting their spirits so they can enjoy life again.
hinglish: "A lift" + "kam karna": Jab aap kisi ka dard alleviate karte hain, toh aap unke dukh ko lift karke kam kar dete hain.

meaning: to make an indirect reference
mnemonic: Allude -> 'All' + 'Dude': when you say 'all dude', you're indirectly referencing all the guys in the room, which is like alluding to them.
hinglish: All + Dude: jab aap 'all dude' kehte hain, toh aap sab mardon ka taraf ishara karte hain, jo allude karne jaisa hai.

meaning: suggestive or implying something indirectly rather than explicitly
mnemonic: "All" + "Loose": if your ideas are all loose, then they're likely allusive, hinting at something without saying it directly — like an allusive poem.
hinglish: "All" + "Loose": agar aapke vichar all loose hain, toh woh allusive hain, bina seedhe kehne ke kuch aur hi samjha rahe hain — jaise ek allusive kavita.

meaning: distant, detached, or uninvolved
mnemonic: "Aloe" + "F" (for friendship): just like an aloe plant remains aloof in a garden, avoiding interaction with other plants, a person can be aloof and not engage socially.
hinglish: "Aloo" + "F" (dosti ke liye): jaise ek aloo khud ko alag rakhta hai, waise hi koi insaan bhi aloof reh sakta hai aur doston se door rehta hai.

meaning: showing selfless concern for the well-being of others
mnemonic: "All True" + "Stick": when you have all true intentions, you stick to being altruistic by helping others without expecting anything in return.
hinglish: "All True" + "Stick": jab aapke sabhi irade sacche hain, toh aap paropkar karne wale bante hain, bina kisi ummeed ke.

meaning: to combine or unite to form one entity
mnemonic: Amal + Gate: if you go through the amal gate, you will amalgamate with the crowd and become one with it.
hinglish: Amal + Gate: agar aap amal gate se guzarte hain, toh aap sabke saath ek ho jaate hain.

meaning: having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something or someone
mnemonic: Ambi + Valence: when you have both positive and negative valences (charges) about a decision, you feel ambivalent.
hinglish: Ambe + Valence: jab aap ek faisle ke liye dono tarah ke jazbat rakhte hain, tab aap ambivalent mehsoos karte hain.

meaning: to make something better or improve it
mnemonic: "A Meal You're Late" -> "Ameliorate": When you arrive late to a dinner, you try to make up for it by bringing a delicious meal to ameliorate the situation.
hinglish: "A Meal You're Late" -> "Ameliorate": Jab aap kisi dinner pe late pauchte hain, toh aap achha khana lekar aate hain taaki aapki galti ko ameliorate kar sakein.

meaning: willing to be influenced or controlled; open to advice or suggestions
mnemonic: Amen + Able: being able to say 'amen' means you're open to agreement or suggestions — she was amenable to new ideas.
hinglish: Amen + Able: agar aap 'amen' kehne ke liye tayyar hain, to aap naye vicharon ke liye bhi amenable hain — voh naye ideas ke liye amenable thi.

meaning: to make changes in order to improve or correct
mnemonic: "A" + "Mend": to amend is to make something better, like taking an 'A' grade and 'mending' it to an 'A+' with corrections.
hinglish: "A" + "Mend": jab aap kisi kaam ko theek karte hain, jaise 'A' grade ko 'A+' banane ke liye sudhar karna, toh aap amend kar rahe hain.

meaning: characterized by friendly goodwill; peaceable
mnemonic: Amicable -> 'Ami' + 'Cable': imagine friends connected by a strong cable, symbolizing an amicable bond that keeps them together.
hinglish: Ami + Cable: soch lo, doston ke beech ek majboot cable hai, jo unhe amicable rakh rahi hai.

meaning: having no definite shape or form
mnemonic: A + Morphous -> A Morphous Creature: imagine a creature that has no fixed shape at all, illustrating the idea of being amorphous.
hinglish: A + Morphoos: socho ek aisa jaanwar jo bilkul bhi shape nahi rakhta, wo hai amorphous.

meaning: to increase the volume or intensity of something
mnemonic: "Ample" + "Fly": when you have an ample amount of sound, it flies through the air, allowing everyone to hear you clearly — to amplify your voice.
hinglish: "Ample" + "Udaan": jab aapke paas kaafi aawaaz ho, to woh udaan bhar kar sab tak pahuchti hai, yani aapki aawaaz amplify hoti hai.

meaning: belonging to a period other than that being portrayed
mnemonic: "Anna" (name) + "Chrono" (time): imagine Anna wearing modern clothes in a historical documentary; her appearance is an anachronistic mismatch for the time period portrayed.
hinglish: "Anna" (नाम) + "Chrono" (समय): socho Anna ek purani film me modern kapde pehne hue hai; yeh anachronistic hai kyunki us samay aise kapde nahi the.

meaning: similar in some way
mnemonic: Analog + Us: when something is analogous, it’s like saying 'it’s analog' to us, meaning it's similar or comparable in function or form — the two concepts are analogous.
hinglish: Ana + Logus: jab do cheezein anjaam ya roop me milti hain, hum kehte hain wo 'ana logus' hain, yaani wo ek dusre se tulnaatmak hain.

meaning: a strong feeling of dislike or hatred
mnemonic: "Animal" + "Silly": imagine a silly animal that can't stand the presence of another, illustrating its animosity. The fierce rivalry between the two animals was filled with animosity.
hinglish: "Janwar" + "Silly": socho ek silly janwar jo dusre se nafrat karta hai, ye uski animosity ko dikhata hai. Dono janwaron ke beech animosity thi, jo kabhi nahi khatam hoti.

meaning: a feeling of animosity or hostility
mnemonic: Annie + Muscles: Annie's muscles were tense and intimidating, reflecting her animus towards her competitor.
hinglish: Annie + Muscles: Annie ke muscles itne tense hain ki woh apne competitor ke liye animus dikhati hai.

meaning: to ceremonially apply oil or another substance as a sign of consecration or blessing
mnemonic: "Aunt" + "Ointment": imagine an aunt applying ointment to bless her favorite niece — she is anointing her with love. Anointing is a ceremonial act of applying oil.
hinglish: "Aunt" + "Ointment": socho ek aunty apni favorite bh niece ko ointment laga rahi hai, woh usse anoint kar rahi hai pyaar se.

meaning: deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected
mnemonic: "A+Nomalous" (Anomalous): When a nomad travels, sometimes they encounter an anomalous situation, like finding a city in the desert.
hinglish: "A+Nomalus" (Anomalous): Jab ek nomad safar karta hai, kabhi kabhi usko aniyamit (anomalous) halat ka samna karna padta hai, jaise registan mein ek sheher milna.

meaning: to provoke someone to react negatively or become hostile
mnemonic: Ant + Agonize: when you make an ant's life difficult, you antagonize it, just like provoking someone.
hinglish: Ant + Ghar: jab aap ek ghar me chidiya ko tang karte hain, toh aap usse antagonize kar rahe hain.

meaning: to precede in time; to occur before something else
mnemonic: "Ante" (before) + "Date" (time): when you antedate a document, you are marking it with a date that comes before the actual date it was created.
hinglish: "Ante" (pehle) + "Date" (tarikh): jab aap kisi document ko antedate karte ho, toh aap us par ek aisi tarikh likhte ho jo asal tarikh se pehle ki hoti hai.

meaning: a strong feeling of dislike or aversion
mnemonic: Anti + Pathy: if you are 'anti' (against) something, you feel a strong antipathy towards it, just like she did with the loud music.
hinglish: Anti + Pathy: agar aap kisi cheez ke 'anti' hain, toh aap uske liye ek strong antipathy mehsoos karte hain, jaise usne loud music ke saath kiya.

meaning: a direct contrast or opposition between two ideas or concepts
mnemonic: Anti + Thesis: if someone presents an anti-thesis, they are placing an idea in direct opposition to a thesis, demonstrating the antithesis of the argument.
hinglish: Anti + Thesis: agar koi kisi thesis ka anti kar raha hai, toh wo uska vipreet khada kar raha hai, jo antithesis hai.

meaning: lack of interest or concern
mnemonic: A + Pathy (path): if you have no interest in a path, you show apathy towards it, refusing to walk it.
hinglish: A + Pathi: agar aapko kisi pathi (path) mein koi dilchaspi nahi hai, toh aap udasinta dikhate hain.

meaning: a pithy observation that contains a general truth
mnemonic: A + For + Ism: an aphorism is like a saying that gives you wisdom in a few words — just like a concise statement.
hinglish: A + For + Ism: ek aphorism aisi baat hoti hai jo kuch shabdon mein hi gyaan deti hai.

meaning: self-confidence or assurance, especially in a demanding situation
mnemonic: "A Plum" -> "Aplomb": Picture someone confidently holding a ripe plum, showing their aplomb in any situation.
hinglish: "A Plum" -> "Aplomb": Ek aadmi ek juicy plum sambhaal raha hai, jaise wo har situation me apne aap par vishwas rakhta hai.

meaning: the highest point in the development of something; the peak
mnemonic: "Apo" (up) + "Gee" (giddy): reaching an apogee can make you feel giddy with success at the highest point of achievement.
hinglish: "Apo" (upar) + "Gee" (khushi): apogee par pahunchne se aap upar khush ho jaate hain jab aapke kaam ka shikhar hota hai.

meaning: a person who argues in favor of something, often used in a defensive context
mnemonic: A + 'polish' + 'it': to polish an argument means to refine and defend it, just like an apologist does.
hinglish: A + 'support' + 'ist': kisi cheez ko support karne waala aadmi ek apologist hota hai.

meaning: to calm or soothe someone by meeting their demands
mnemonic: A + Peace: to achieve peace with someone, you must appease them by addressing their concerns.
hinglish: A + Peace: kisi se shanti prapt karne ke liye, aapko unki baatein sun kar appease karna padega.

meaning: relevant and appropriate
mnemonic: "Apposite" -> "Opposite" + "Site": when you visit the opposite site of a topic, your thoughts must be apposite to remain relevant in discussions.
hinglish: "Apposite" -> "Opposite" + "Sait": jab aap kisi conversation mein opposite site par hote hain, toh aapke vichar apposite (उचित) hone chahiye.

meaning: a feeling of anxiety or fear about the future
mnemonic: "Apprehend" -> "Apre-hension" (a pre-hension or pre-capture): when you catch a glimpse of something scary before it happens, it creates a sense of apprehension about the future.
hinglish: "Apre" (aap pehle) + "Hension" (tension): jab aap pehle se kisi cheez ki tension mehsoos karte ho, to wo apprehension hoti hai.

meaning: to inform or notify someone
mnemonic: App + Rise: when you appraise someone, you help them rise by providing necessary information — they are apprised of what’s happening.
hinglish: Aap + Rise: jab aap kisi ko update dete hain, toh unhe madad milti hai aage badhne ke liye — unhe apprise karte hain.

meaning: approval or praise
mnemonic: App + Robation: when you get an 'app' (application) approved, it's like receiving approbation for your work.
hinglish: App + Robation: jab aapka application 'app' ke roop mein swikar hota hai, toh aapko uski swikriti ya approbation milti hai.

meaning: suitable or proper in the circumstances
mnemonic: "A Propriate" -> "A Proper Eight": think of a group of eight friends choosing a proper outfit for an occasion; they discuss and decide on the appropriate attire.
hinglish: "A Propriate" -> "A Proper Eight": socho aath dost ek sath milke kisi occasion ke liye appropriate dress choose kar rahe hain.

meaning: relevant to the situation; appropriate
mnemonic: "A Pro" + "Pose": if you're a pro, your pose is always apropos, meaning it's appropriate for any situation. His advice was apropos to the topic we were discussing.
hinglish: "A Pro" + "Pos": agar aap pro hain, toh aapka pose hamesha apropos hota hai, matlab har situation ke liye sahi hota hai. Uska sujhav humare discussion ke liye apropos tha.

meaning: appropriate or suitable in the circumstances
mnemonic: Apt -> Aptitude: having a natural aptitude means you are appropriately skilled, making it apt for the task.
hinglish: Apt + T: jab koi skill ke liye apt (uchit) hota hai, toh wo task ke liye perfect hota hai.

meaning: based on random choice or personal whim, rather than any reason or system
mnemonic: Arbit + Rare Tea: if you choose a rare tea on a whim without any reason, your choice is arbitrary.
hinglish: Arbit + Roti: agar aap bina kisi wajah ke roti chunte hain, toh aapka faisla manmanya hai.

meaning: known or understood by very few; secret or mysterious
mnemonic: "Arcane" -> "Our Cane": if our cane is hidden, it's arcane, understood only by us; just like the arcane secrets of magic that few can comprehend.
hinglish: "Ar" + "Kain": agar hamari cane chhupi hui hai, to wo arcane hai, sirf humein samajh aata hai; jaise kuch arcane raaz jo sirf kuch hi log samajhte hain.

meaning: belonging to an earlier period; outdated
mnemonic: "Arc" (curve) + "Haic" (like hiccup): the arc of history can seem like a hiccup when you realize how archaic some of our customs have become.
hinglish: "Arc" (ukhadna) + "Haic" (jaise hiccup): itna purana hai ki humare kuch riti-rivaj archaic ho gaye hain, bilkul arc ki tarah joh kabhi ukhad jaata hai.

meaning: a typical example or pattern of something; a model
mnemonic: Arch + Type: an 'arch' (chief) 'type' is the original model or archetype for all others, like a classic hero.
hinglish: Arch + Type: ek 'arch' (mukhya) 'type' ka matlab hota hai sabse pehla udaharan ya archetype, jaise ek classic hero.

meaning: enthusiastic or passionate
mnemonic: 'Art' + 'Dent': If an artist is passionate about their craft, they create ardent masterpieces that leave a mark, like a dent in your heart.
hinglish: 'Art' + 'Dent': Agar ek artist apne kaam ke liye ardent hai, toh wo aise masterpieces banata hai jo dil par ek dent kar dete hain.

meaning: involving or requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring
mnemonic: Arduous -> 'Hard Work': the arduous journey through the jungle required hard work and determination from all the team members.
hinglish: Arduous -> 'Hard Work': woh arduous safar jo humein jungle se guzarne pada, usme bahut hard work ki zarurat thi.

meaning: striking or eye-catching; attracting attention
mnemonic: "A Resting" -> "A Resting Place": a place that makes you stop and look because it's so beautiful is arresting.
hinglish: "A Resting" + "Place": ek aisa jagah jo dekhne par aapko rukhne par majboor kare, wahi hai arresting.

meaning: skilled at achieving one's aims by indirect or deceitful methods
mnemonic: "Art" + "Full": being full of art means being clever in a creative way; the artful thief had a plan full of clever tricks.
hinglish: "Art" + "Full": jab koi chori karne ke liye art se bharpoor plan banata hai, toh woh artful hota hai.

meaning: able to express thoughts and ideas clearly and effectively
mnemonic: 'Art' + 'I' + 'Culate' (to calculate): if you can calculate art, you can articulate your artistic thoughts easily.
hinglish: 'Art' + 'I' + 'Culate': agar aap art ko calculate kar sakte hain, toh aap apne vichar ko articulate kar sakte hain.

meaning: lacking artifice or deceit; natural and simple
mnemonic: "Art" + "Less": without any artifice or trickery, her artless approach was refreshing and genuine.
hinglish: "Art" + "Less": bina kisi jhoot ya chalakiyon ke, uski artless baatein sabko apni taraf kheench leti thi.

meaning: to find out or learn with certainty
mnemonic: "Ass" + "Certain": When you want to ascertain something, you make sure (become certain) about it, just like an ass (donkey) stubbornly sticking to its point until it's confirmed.
hinglish: "Ass" + "Certain": Jab aap kisi cheez ko ascertain karna chahte hain, toh aap us cheez ki confirmation karte hain, bilkul jaise ek gadha apni baat par ziddi hota hai jab tak sach nahi milta.

meaning: one who leads a life of strict self-discipline and abstention from indulgence
mnemonic: "A + Set + Tick": an ascetic has a 'set' routine without any 'ticks' of pleasure or distractions, focusing solely on self-discipline.
hinglish: "A + Set + Tick": ek ascetic apni zindagi ko 'set' karta hai jahan wo kisi 'tick' (maza) se door rehta hai, sirf atma-samarpan par dhyan deta hai.

meaning: to attribute something to a cause or source
mnemonic: As + Scribe: when you write (or scribe) something down, you often ascribe it to a particular source or person.
hinglish: As + Scribe: jab aap kisi cheez ko likhte hain, to aap uska ascribe karte hain kisika naam ya source ko.

meaning: a false or misleading charge meant to harm someone's reputation
mnemonic: Aspersion -> 'A Spurt in' (liquid): when you make a spurt of water on someone, you’re casting aspersions on them, just like a false accusation.
hinglish: Aspersh -> 'A Spurt' (chhidakna): jab aap kisike upar paani chhidakte hain, aap us par aspersions daal rahe hote hain, jaise jhooti ilzaam.

meaning: to attack violently or with words
mnemonic: Assail -> 'Ass' + 'Sail': imagine an ass throwing a sail at someone in anger, thus to assail them with an attack.
hinglish: Ass + Sail: ek ass ek sail ko kisi par fenk raha hai, jo unhe humla karne ja raha hai.

meaning: having or showing a confident and forceful personality
mnemonic: "Assert" + "ive": being assertive means you assert your opinions and rights confidently in discussions.
hinglish: "Aasert" + "ive": jab aap akele hi sab kuch kehne me aasert ho toh aap assertive hai.

meaning: to make an unpleasant feeling less intense
mnemonic: Ass + Wage: if you pay your dues (wage) to someone you hurt, you can assuage the pain you caused. — Assuaging guilt is like paying a toll to ease your conscience.
hinglish: Ass + Wage: agar aap kisi ki galti ka bhugtan karte hain (wage), to aap us dard ko kam kar sakte hain. — Apology se dukh ko assuage karna asaan hota hai.

meaning: having a sharp or bitter taste or smell; causing a tightening or constriction of body tissues
mnemonic: "A String Tent" -> "A String" + "Tent" (a tight structure): When you taste something astringent, it feels like the taste is tightening your mouth like a string holding a tent in place.
hinglish: "A String" + "Tent": jab aap astringent khate hain, toh aapka munh tight feel hota hai jaise ek string se tent bandh diya gaya ho.

meaning: having or showing an ability to accurately assess situations or people and turn this to one's advantage
mnemonic: Astute -> A Suit: if you wear a sharp suit, people will think you are astute and savvy in business matters.
hinglish: Aas + Toot: agar aap aasani se toot jaate hain toh chatur (astute) hona zaroori hai.

meaning: to reduce in force, intensity, or severity
mnemonic: "At Ten You Ate": if you eat a lot at ten, you might feel too full, but if you eat a little, you can attenuate your hunger. The doctor advised to attenuate my appetite for better health.
hinglish: "At Ten You Ate": agar aapne 10 baje bahut khana khaya, toh aapko bhookh kam karne ke liye attenuate karna padega.

meaning: a quality or feature regarded as a characteristic or inherent part of someone or something
mnemonic: "A Tribute" -> "Attribute": when you pay a tribute, you highlight an important attribute or quality of someone.
hinglish: "A Tribute" -> "Attribute": jab aap kisi ko tribute dete hain, toh aap unki important attribute ko highlight karte hain.

meaning: showing a willingness to take surprisingly bold risks
mnemonic: Audacious -> 'Audio' + 'Cious' (like cautious): If you're too 'cious' (cautious), you'll never be audacious enough to take risks.
hinglish: Audio + Cious: Agar aap zyada 'cious' (cautious) hain, toh aap kabhi bhi audacious (sahasi) nahi ban sakte.

meaning: to increase or make something larger
mnemonic: Augment -> 'Aug' (like the month) + 'Ment' (to join): in August, you might augment your garden by planting more flowers.
hinglish: Aug + Ment: August me tum apne garden ko augment karte ho zyada phool laga kar.

meaning: having great dignity or grandeur
mnemonic: "Awe" + "Gust": when you see something awe-inspiring like an august monument, you feel a gust of admiration. It was such an august building that everyone stopped to admire it.
hinglish: "Awe" + "Gust": jab aap kisi awe-inspiring cheez ko dekhte hain jaise ek august mahal, toh aapko admiration ka ek gust mehsoos hota hai. Woh itna august tha ki log use dekhte reh gaye.

meaning: conducive to success; favorable
mnemonic: Awe + Spicious: when you see something awe-inspiring, it feels auspicious for good things to come.
hinglish: Awe + Shubh: jab aap kuch awe-inspiring dekhte hain, to wo aapke liye shubh (auspicious) mehsoos hota hai.

meaning: severe or strict in manner, attitude, or appearance
mnemonic: "Awe" + "Steer": to create an awe-inspiring discipline, one must steer clear of luxuries, leading to an austere lifestyle.
hinglish: "Aas" + "Tere": jab tum aas se door hote ho, tab tumhare jeevan mein aise sikhshak hote hain jo sadharan aur austere hote hain.

meaning: providing supplementary or additional support
mnemonic: Auxiliary -> 'Ox + Hill': imagine an ox helping to carry a heavy load up a hill, just like auxiliary support helps ease the burden of a task.
hinglish: Ox + Hill: ek ox jab ek hill par chadhne mein madad karta hai, waise hi auxiliary support kisi kaam ko asaan karne ke liye hota hai.

meaning: having or showing an excessive desire for wealth or gain
mnemonic: "Avarice" -> "A Very Rich": a person who is avaricious is someone who is always wanting to become very rich, often at the expense of others.
hinglish: "Avarice" -> "A Very Rich": jo vyakti aavaricious hota hai, wo har haal mein bahut paisa kamaana chahta hai, kabhi kabhi doosron ko nuqsan pohchaakar.

meaning: to assert or affirm with confidence
mnemonic: "A" + "Ver" (like 'aver'): to aver means to confidently declare, just as a lawyer might aver their client's innocence.
hinglish: "A" + "Ver" (jaise 'aver'): voh apne be-gunaah hone ka aver karti hai, jaise ek lawyer apne client ki masoomiyat ka daawa karta hai.

meaning: a strong dislike or repugnance
mnemonic: "Averse" + "ion": an ion that is negative tends to have an aversion to things that are positive, just like she has an aversion to spicy food.
hinglish: "Averse" + "ion": jab kisi cheez se aap kaafi door bhaagte hain, toh aapko us cheez se aversion hota hai, jaise usse spicy khaana nahi pasand.

meaning: to prevent something from happening
mnemonic: A + 'Vert' (turn): when you avert your eyes, you turn away from something unpleasant, allowing you to prevent it from affecting you.
hinglish: A + 'Wart' (disease): agar aap ek wart ko dekhne se avert karte hain, toh aap usse khud par hone wale nuksan se rok sakte hain.

meaning: having or showing a keen interest in or enthusiasm for something
mnemonic: Avi + D: an aviator is an avid lover of flying, as he shows great enthusiasm for the sky.
hinglish: Avi + D: aviator mein avi dikhata hai ki woh udan ka deewana hai.

meaning: self-evident or unquestionable
mnemonic: Axe + I +omatic: If you take an axe to a problem, it's axiomatic that you'll solve it quickly — obvious to anyone.
hinglish: Axe + I +omatic: Agar aap kisi masle ko axe se kaat rahe hain, toh ye to svatah spasht hai ki aap ise jaldi hal karenge — sabke liye obvious hai.

meaning: lacking in originality, freshness, or novelty; trite
mnemonic: "Ban" + "All": ban all creativity and you end up with banal ideas that are dull and uninteresting: the movie was so banal that I quickly lost interest and fell asleep.
hinglish: "Ban" + "All": sabhi creativity ko ban kar do aur aap banal ideas paoge jo bilkul bekar hote hain: wo film itni banal thi ki main jaldi hi bore ho gaya aur so gaya.

meaning: to send someone away from a place as a punishment
mnemonic: Ban + Ish: to ban someone is to send them away like in a game where you banish a player from the match.
hinglish: Ban + Ish: jab aap kisi ko chhodne ka faisla karte hain, tab aap usse 'banish' karte hain jaise kisi ko khel se bahar kar dena.

meaning: characterized by extravagant detail and elaborate ornamentation, often in art and architecture
mnemonic: Baroque -> 'Bar Rock': imagine a rock that is adorned with extravagant decorations, just like baroque art is filled with elaborate details.
hinglish: Bar + Rock: socho ek pathar par itne saare sajawat hai, jaise baroque kala mein har jagah bhari bhari design hote hain.

meaning: a concentrated artillery bombardment over a wide area
mnemonic: "Bar" + "Rage": when you’re at the bar and get into a rage, you let out a barrage of insults to everyone around — just like a barrage of artillery fire.
hinglish: "Bar" + "Rage": jab aap bar mein hote hain aur gusse mein aa jaate hain, aap sab par ek saath baarish ki tarah galiyaan bechte hain, jaise ek barrage.

meaning: not fertile or productive; unproductive land
mnemonic: Bar + Ren: if you have a 'bar' in a 'ren' (rain), it suggests a lack of fertility; thus, the barren land is dry and unproductive.
hinglish: Bar + Rain: agar baarish nahi hoti to zameen barren ho jati hai, jisse kisan kuch nahi uga sakte.

meaning: the foundation or support of something
mnemonic: Base -> 'Base' + 'Space': the base is the space at the bottom where everything stands, just like the base of a tall building.
hinglish: Base + Space: base wo jagah hai jahan sab kuch khada hota hai, jaise ek buildings ke base par.

meaning: humorously indecent or obscene
mnemonic: Bawdy -> 'Bawdy' sounds like 'Body': a body can be involved in bawdy humor when it's depicted in an indecent or obscene manner.
hinglish: Body + Bawdy: body ka mazak aise hota hai jo ashliil ho, jaise bawdy chhote jokes party mein hote hain.

meaning: confused or perplexed
mnemonic: Be + Fuddled: if you 'be' in a 'fuddle' (a mess), you will be befuddled and unable to think clearly.
hinglish: Be + Fuddled: agar aap 'be' karte hain aur 'fuddle' (mess) mein hain, toh aap befuddled ho jaate hain aur soch nahi paate.

meaning: to charm or enchant someone, often in a deceptive way
mnemonic: "Be Guy" -> "Be Getting You Lured": if you want to be a guy who charms everyone, you might beguile them with your wit and charm.
hinglish: "Be Guy" -> "Be Getting You Lured": agar aap aise ladke banne ki koshish karte ho jo sabko apni baaton se behka de, toh aap unhein beguile kar rahe ho.

meaning: owing thanks or having a duty to someone
mnemonic: Be + Hold + En: when you behold (hold) something beautiful, you often feel beholden to the creator for that gift.
hinglish: Be + Hold + En: jab aap kisi sundar cheez ko dekhte hain, tab aap uske creator ke liye kirdar mehsoos karte hain, yahaan aap kirdar hain.

meaning: to contradict or show something to be false
mnemonic: Be + Lie: to 'be' a lie means to show a contradiction; the news reports belied the truth of the situation.
hinglish: Be + Lie: jab aap sach ke bajaye jhooth bolte hain, tab aapki baatein sachai ko bhromak kar deti hain, jaise unhone aisa kiya.

meaning: Make someone or something seem unimportant.
mnemonic: "Be + Little": Treating someone like a little child to ruin their confidence.

meaning: Hostile and aggressive.
mnemonic: "Belly-fight": Think of two sumo wrestlers puffing out their bellies, ready to launch into an aggressive fight.

meaning: A standard or point of reference against which things may be compared.
mnemonic: "Bench-Mark": Drawing a clear mark on a bench to measure everyone's height against a set standard.

meaning: Resulting in good; doing good.
mnemonic: "Benefit-Cent": A kind act that provides 100 cents of benefit to poor families.

meaning: Well meaning and kindly.
mnemonic: "Bene-Violent (Antonym)": The exact opposite of violent; a gentle person who always wishes you well.

meaning: Gentle and kindly; harmless.
mnemonic: "Be + Nice": A tumor or condition that turns out to be nice and completely safe.

meaning: Scold or criticize someone angrily.
mnemonic: "Buri-Rate": A furious father giving his son a buri rate (terrible review) and scolding him for failing.

meaning: Deprived of or lacking something.
mnemonic: "Bear-Left": A traveler left completely alone in the woods after his protective bear left him.

meaning: Unfaithfully break a trust.
mnemonic: "Beech-Rasta": Abandoning your best friend in the beech-rasta (middle of the road) to join the rival team.

meaning: Spoiled, harmed, or destroyed.
mnemonic: "Black-Light": A dark, toxic black light that ruins and dries up a beautiful crop overnight.

meaning: Showing a casual and cheerful indifference.
mnemonic: "Bliss-ful": Being so happy and blissful that you don't care about tomorrow's deadlines.

meaning: Not genuine or true; fake.
mnemonic: "Bogus-Bonus": A scam email promising a fake bonus just to steal your bank password.

meaning: Noisy, energetic, and cheerful; rowdy.
mnemonic: "Boy-Stir": A group of young boys stirring up a storm, shouting and dancing wildly at a concert.

meaning: Support or strengthen; prop up.
mnemonic: "Pillow-Bolster": Placing a heavy round bolster pillow behind your back to give you solid sitting support.

meaning: High-sounding but with little meaning; inflated.
mnemonic: "Bomb-Plastic": A politician throwing verbal bombs in his speech, but the content is empty plastic.

meaning: A thing that is helpful or beneficial.
mnemonic: "Bonus": Getting a massive unexpected bonus from your company that solves all your money problems.

meaning: Rough and bad-mannered; coarse.
mnemonic: "Bore-ish": A rude person at a dinner party who acts so boorish that he becomes a total bore.

meaning: A bold manner or a show of boldness intended to impress or intimidate.
mnemonic: "Bravo-Fake": Yelling "Bravo!" loudly to act brave, even though your knees are shaking from fear.

meaning: Bold and without shame.
mnemonic: "Brass-Zen": A person with a face as hard as solid brass who commits a crime in broad daylight without blinking.

meaning: Concise and exact use of words in writing or speech.
mnemonic: "Brief-ity": Delivering a complex coding breakdown with absolute briefness, keeping it straight to the point.

meaning: Show resentment or anger; bring under control.
mnemonic: "Bride-Anger": A horse throwing its head back in rage when the bridle (lagaam) is pulled tightly.

meaning: A trite and unoriginal remark, typically intended to soothe or placate.
mnemonic: "Boring-Idea": A cliché, boring phrase like "everything happens for a reason" that makes you yawn.

meaning: Tolerate or allow.
mnemonic: "Brave-it": A strict professor who will not brook (tolerate) any cheating in his classroom.

meaning: Relating to the pleasant aspects of the countryside and country life.
mnemonic: "Bull-Colony": A beautiful, peaceful village full of green fields and farms where bulls roam freely.

meaning: Able or apt to stay afloat or rise to the top; cheerful.
mnemonic: "Boy-Ant": An ant floating happily on a leaf in water, completely upbeat and unsinkable.

meaning: Begin to grow or increase rapidly; flourish.
mnemonic: "Burger-Shop": A new burger joint that opens up and rapidly expands into 50 branches within a month.

meaning: Polish (something, especially metal) by rubbing.
mnemonic: "Burn-to-Shine": Rubbing a metallic shield so hard it looks like it's burning with pure shine.

meaning: A source of defense or support.
mnemonic: "Butt-Rest": Building a solid brick pillar to give a leaning wall a place to rest and stay strong.

meaning: Excessively complex, typically involving a great deal of administrative detail.
mnemonic: "Busy-Teenagers": A government system so tangled and complex that it keeps thousands of teenagers busy trying to figure it out.

meaning: Involving or producing a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds.
mnemonic: "Cackling-Crow": A thousand crows cackling together outside your bedroom window at 4 AM — terrible sound.

meaning: Persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing or flattery.
mnemonic: "Kajol-Fan": Flattering a stubborn developer like a star struck fan to cajole them into deploying your code.

meaning: Involving or causing sudden great damage or distress.
mnemonic: "Kaal-amity": A massive natural disaster that brings absolute kaal (destruction) to a town.

meaning: Showing or having an insensitive and cruel disregard for others.
mnemonic: "Calm-in-Loss": A cruel person who remains completely calm during someone else's loss, showing no emotion.

meaning: Inexperienced and immature.
mnemonic: "Cal-low (Caliber-low)": A young rookie coder whose caliber is currently low because he just started today.

meaning: The making of false and defamatory statements about someone.
mnemonic: "Kala-Naam": Spreading nasty lies to put a kala daag (black stain) on an innocent person's reputation.

meaning: Truthful and straightforward; frank.
mnemonic: "Candy-Child": A small kid who will tell you honestly if your app design looks bad in exchange for a candy.

meaning: Having or showing shrewdness and good judgment, especially in money.
mnemonic: "Can-i-Know": A sharp businessman who always asks, "Can I know the exact profit margin?" before investing.

meaning: Treat as holy or benign; place in the canon of saints.
hindi: Pavitra ghoshit karna / Sir par bithana
mnemonic: "Canon-Camera": Treating a legendary photographer so highly you want to frame his photo with a Canon camera.

meaning: Cease to resist an opponent or an unwelcome demand; surrender.
mnemonic: "Captain-Late": The army captain arrived too late, forcing the remaining soldiers to finally surrender.

meaning: Given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood.
mnemonic: "Car-Price": Market trends that fluctuate wildly, causing a car's price to jump up and down without warning.

meaning: Tending to find fault or raise petty objections.
mnemonic: "Captain-Strict": An annoying tester who is always capturing minor bugs just to complain.

meaning: A picture or description of a person in which certain characteristics are exaggerated.
mnemonic: "Character-Cartoon": Drawing a politician's character as a funny cartoon with a giant nose.

meaning: Reprimand someone severely.
mnemonic: "Cast-Gate": Throwing a lazy guard out of the caste gate and scolding him brutally for sleeping.

meaning: Relating to or denoting a violent natural event.
mnemonic: "Cut-a-Climate": A volcanic eruption so violent it completely cuts and alters the climate of the region.

meaning: Involving or causing sudden great damage or suffering.
mnemonic: "Crash-Trophy": Your racing car crashing right before the trophy line — a total disaster.

meaning: Providing psychological relief through the open expression of strong emotions.
mnemonic: "Cat-Heart": Crying out all your worries while holding a pet cat close to your heart, feeling immediate relief.

meaning: Sarcastic in a scathing and bitter way; able to burn.
mnemonic: "Chemical-Acid": A comment so sharp it burns your ears like caustic soda burns skin.

meaning: Showing a lack of proper concern; offhand.
mnemonic: "Cavalry-Soldier": An elite soldier riding a horse who looks down on common pedestrians with careless arrogance.

meaning: Bring or come to an end.
mnemonic: "Ceasefire": An official command to instantly stop all shooting on the battlefield.

meaning: Examine officially and suppress unacceptable parts.
mnemonic: "Sensor-Cut": The regulatory board placing a sensor block over inappropriate movie scenes.

meaning: Express severe disapproval of, typically in a formal statement.
mnemonic: "Sensor-Reject": The official board passing a formal censure motion to condemn a bad book.

meaning: Intellectual rather than emotional or physical.
mnemonic: "Brain-Cerebrum": Using your cerebrum (the main part of the brain) to solve complex system architectures.

meaning: Annoyance or distress at having failed or been humiliated.
mnemonic: "Chai-Gir-Gayi": The deep embarrassment you feel when your chai spills on your white shirt during a client meet.

meaning: Vigorously defend or support a cause.
mnemonic: "Champion for Poor": Acting like a real sports champion who uses their fame to fight for equal rights.

meaning: Cautiously or suspiciously reluctant to do something.
mnemonic: "Chai-se-Jala": Like the Hindi proverb: Chai ka jala chach bhi phook kar peeta hai — extremely cautious.

meaning: Rebuke or reprimand severely.
mnemonic: "Chest-Tight": A strict drill sergeant scolding a soldier so hard that the rookie's chest tightens with fear.

meaning: Displaying excessive or prejudiced loyalty or support for a cause, group, or gender.
mnemonic: "Chauhan-Proud": A warrior who blindly believes his group (Chauhans) is superior to the entire world.

meaning: Stop or slow down the progress of something.
mnemonic: "Check-Dam": Building a temporary wall to check the rapid flow of wild river water.

meaning: Protect and care for someone lovingly; hold dear.
mnemonic: "Cherry-on-Top": Keeping a special childhood memory safely in your heart like the best cherry on a cake.

meaning: The use of trickery to achieve a political, financial, or legal purpose.
mnemonic: "Chic-Chalaak": A shady lawyer using clever hera-pheri and shortcuts to win a corporate court case.

meaning: Courteous and gallant, especially toward women.
mnemonic: "Chevalier (Knight)": An honorable knight who rushes to open the door and protect someone in need.

meaning: Rude in a mean-spirited and surly way.
mnemonic: "Church-Rude": An ill-mannered tourist shouting and acting extremely rude inside a quiet church.

meaning: Restrict something within limits.
mnemonic: "Circle-Scribe": Drawing a strict circle on paper and telling someone, "You cannot step outside this line."

meaning: Wary and unwilling to take risks.
mnemonic: "Circle-Inspect": Looking all around your circle to inspect for dangers before taking a single step.

meaning: Pointing indirectly toward someone's guilt but not conclusively proving it.
mnemonic: "Circumstance-Only": Evidence based purely on the surrounding circumstances, not solid eye-witness proof.

meaning: Making a loud and confused noise.
mnemonic: "Claim-Loud": A massive crowd of angry protestors loudly claiming their rights outside the assembly.

meaning: Kept secret or done secretively, especially because illicit.
mnemonic: "Clan-Destiny": A secret meeting held by a hidden clan at midnight to plan their next move.

meaning: A continuous loud banging or ringing sound.
mnemonic: "Clan-of-Gongs": A huge group of people banging metal gongs together in a closed room.

meaning: Hide, cover, or disguise.
mnemonic: "Invisibility Cloak": Putting on a Harry Potter cloak to disappear from your enemies completely.

meaning: Excessively sweet, rich, or sentimental to the point of disgusting.
mnemonic: "Clog-with-Sugar": A dessert so heavy and overly sweet that it literally clogs your throat after one bite.

meaning: A group of similar things or people positioned closely together.
mnemonic: "Star-Cluster": A dense group of stars packed closely together in one part of the sky.

meaning: Come together to form one mass or whole.
mnemonic: "Coal-Mix": Small pieces of hot coal melting and merging together to form one giant fire block.

meaning: Treat in an indulgent or overprotective way.
